passage: Jomon here, Seema's classmate. We were both at the college junction on Tuesday when an auto nudged a scooter. Nobody was hurt; the scooter rider just picked up a broken mirror. That night our class group chat was full of it. A forwarded post said the auto driver was on his phone and jumped the red. By Thursday, Seema was telling our lab partners the whole thing: "I saw him on the phone, he didn't even look." She said it with total certainty, tapping the table. I didn't see a phone. I remember both hands on the handlebar and the light turning amber. When I said so, she laughed. "You were looking at your chai." Maybe I was. But she was looking at the scooter first; I saw her turn. I don't know what she saw. I only know her version grew after the chat.

Our hostel buzzed with it, everyone adding a crying boy, a bleeding knee. For thirty years I told that story, and I could see the boy: his blue shorts, his lost tiffin box. Then at a reunion Usha laughed. "Sonali, there was no boy. I was holding your arm. We watched a wheel roll into the drain." I went home that night and could still see those blue shorts. So now, beta, I say "I think."

qa.a: To say "I think" more often, which leaves room for the chance that even a vivid memory is wrong.

Internship supervisor's note, 14 July

On Monday our intern Eshaan saw a delivery van reverse into a parked cycle outside the office. He came in shaken and said, 'The van just backed into it, slowly.' By Wednesday, after the videos in the office group and a post on the local news page, his version had changed: the driver was speeding, on his phone, and swore at the cyclist. When the building manager asked him to write a statement, he included all of it and said he was '100% sure'. I asked Eshaan, gently, to tell me only what he saw with his own eyes. He was quiet, then said, 'Slow reverse. That's all I saw.' I have asked him to rewrite the statement with just that, and to mark anything else as 'heard later'.

Lokesh

Around four, near the college gate, a scooter clipped an auto. I was on the steps, half blind with gulal, and heard the crunch more than saw it. Nobody was hurt, just a bent mirror and a lot of shouting.
Tonight the colony group is full of it. Someone posted a local news clip saying the scooter guy was racing and on his phone. Nazia texted, "Gautam, you were right there, was he on the phone?" And yes. I can see it now, the phone pressed to his ear, the speed. I wrote back, "100%, he was."
Funny, I didn't mention a phone to anyone this afternoon. But I'm sure. Totally sure.
